statement: In laboratory tests of urine fentanyl test strips on single fentanyl analogues dissolved in water, compared with the known content of each solution, the strips reacted to most analogues tested, many of them only at concentrations well above those at which they detect fentanyl, and to a few not at all. With four brands and 28 analogues read once by the authors (no test band or a barely visible one counted as positive), 21, 19, 15 and 22 analogues read positive at 1000 ng/mL and 24, 24, 21 and 24 at up to 10 000 ng/mL, but only 5, 5, 12 and 9 of the 23 measured at 100 ng/mL; under the makers' rule, which counts any visible test band as negative, fewer were positive (editors' recount on the study card: 20, 20, 19 and 21 of 28 at the highest concentrations). No brand detected alfentanil, despropionyl-2-fluorofentanyl or norcarfentanil; carfentanil gave at most a faint band at 1000 ng/mL, read positive at 4000 ng/mL on three brands, and never on the fourth (Bergh et al., 2021). Five lots of one brand all detected 11 of the 13 analogues tested, carfentanil among them, with limits that differed between lots; sufentanil was detected only by lots obtained in 2017, and no lot detected alfentanil or the non-fentanyl opioid U-47700 at up to 10 µg/mL (Halifax et al., 2024). In four police-seized samples containing acetyl fentanyl or furanyl fentanyl, one brand read positive in all four (Green et al., 2020). Four analogues too dilute to show alone (10 ng/mL each) read positive when mixed, on the one brand tested (Bergh et al.). A scoping review relays that carfentanil, norcarfentanil and norfentanyl test negative (Kutscher et al., 2024, second-hand), which for carfentanil differs from the two laboratory studies read here. The analogue panels were not chosen by how often each compound occurs in drug markets, and results came from pure compounds rather than mixtures. Certainty: very low. Status: replicated.
plain: In laboratory tests, fentanyl strips reacted to most drugs related to fentanyl, but some only in larger amounts than fentanyl itself, and a few never. Carfentanil showed up only in large amounts, and never on one of four brands. These were pure drugs in water, read once by laboratory staff.
population: Single fentanyl analogues dissolved in water at set concentrations (28 analogues in one study, 13 in another) and four police-seized samples containing analogues
exposure: Urine fentanyl test strips (four brands in one study; five lots of one brand in another), read by laboratory staff
comparator: Known content of each solution; earlier GC/MS for the seized samples
outcome: Whether each analogue made the strip read positive, and at which concentration
magnitude: Bergh et al. (authors' rule): at 100 ng/mL Rapid Response 5, Rapid Self Test 5, One Step 12, Nal van Minden 9 of 23 measured; at 1000 ng/mL 21, 19, 15 and 22 of 28; cumulative to 10 000 ng/mL 24, 24, 21 and 24 of 28; makers' rule (editors' recount on the card): 1, 2, 11 and 4 of 23 at 100 ng/mL, 20, 20, 19 and 21 of 28 cumulative. Carfentanil: faint (three brands) or negative (One Step) at 1000 ng/mL, positive at 4000 ng/mL on three brands. Halifax et al.: 11 analogues on all five lots; sufentanil on 2017 lots only; alfentanil and U-47700 not detected up to 10 µg/mL. Green et al.: 4 of 4 seized analogue samples positive.

evidence.locator: Table 1, summary rows and note a (p. 2); Results › Selectivity of fentanyl test strips, 1st paragraph; Results › Sensitivity of fentanyl test strips, 1st paragraph (p. 3)
evidence.extracted: Four brands dipped in single-analogue solutions of 28 analogues in Type 1 water, graded by the authors (++ no test band and + barely visible band, both counted positive; (+) faint; − solid band). Positive at 1000 ng/mL: Rapid Response 21, Rapid Self Test 19, One Step 15, Nal van Minden 22 of 28; cumulatively up to 10 000 ng/mL: 24, 24, 21 and 24; at 100 ng/mL: 5, 5, 12 and 9. Never positive on any brand: alfentanil, despropionyl-2-fluorofentanyl and norcarfentanil; remifentanil at most weak or ambiguous. Editors' count: five analogues were not measured at 100 ng/mL but are counted negative in the table, so those counts are of 23; by the makers' rule (only no test band positive) the cumulative counts are 20, 20, 19 and 21 of 28 (recount of Table 1 on the study card, checked for Rapid Response).

evidence.locator: Table 1, carfentanil row and note b (p. 2); Results › Sensitivity of fentanyl test strips, 2nd paragraph (p. 3)
evidence.extracted: No brand was positive for carfentanil at 1000 ng/mL (three faint or ambiguous, One Step negative); Rapid Response, Rapid Self Test and Nal van Minden read positive at 4000 ng/mL, a concentration the authors chose from a cited estimate that 20 μg of carfentanil in 5 mL is potentially life-threatening; One Step read negative at every concentration tested.

evidence.locator: Results › Additive effect of fentanyl analogues for test strip results, 1st paragraph
evidence.extracted: Acetyl-, acryl-, furanyl- and butyrfentanyl at 10 ng/mL each read negative or weak alone but positive as a mixture of the four; shown with Nal van Minden only, and expected by the authors, not shown, to hold for all brands.
evidence.source_read: PDF PDFs/Fentanyl-and-analogues/Bergh_2021_FTS_SelectivitySensitivity.pdf (no printed page numbers; PDF pages)

evidence.locator: Methods › Strip sensitivity and cross-reactivity, 1st paragraph; Results › Fentanyl test strip sensitivity and cross-reactivity, 1st and 2nd paragraphs
evidence.extracted: Fentanyl, 13 fentanyl analogues and U-47700 in water at 10 µg/mL down to 10 ng/mL, in duplicate on five lots: all lots cross-reacted with 11 analogues (3-methylfentanyl, acetyl fentanyl, acrylfentanyl, β-hydroxy-thiofentanyl, butyrylfentanyl, carfentanil, cyclopropylfentanyl, fluorobutyrylfentanyl, furanyl fentanyl, p-fluorofentanyl and tetrahydrofuran fentanyl); the 2017 lots also detected sufentanil and the 2021 lots did not; no lot detected alfentanil or U-47700 at any concentration tested (highest 10 µg/mL). Per-lot limits appear only in a figure; the 2021 lots were less sensitive than the 2017 lots for acrylfentanyl (except one lot), butyrylfentanyl and carfentanil, and 10 to 50 times more sensitive for acetyl fentanyl, β-hydroxy-thiofentanyl, furanyl fentanyl and p-fluorofentanyl.
evidence.located_by: AI reader 139 (first reader), from AI reader 138's study card

evidence.extracted: Four police-seized samples containing acetyl fentanyl alone (2), furanyl fentanyl alone (1) or furanyl fentanyl with heroin (1): the strip detected fentanyl presence in all four, while the Raman direct scan was inconclusive in all and a counterfeit pill with furanyl fentanyl was missed by both Raman and FTIR.

evidence.locator: Results › FTS accuracy and reliability, 1st paragraph
evidence.extracted: Relays, without appraisal, that only some analogues test positive, such as acetyl fentanyl and furanylfentanyl, while carfentanil, norcarfentanil and norfentanyl test negative (references 15, 16, 25 and 26).
evidence.source_read: PDF PDFs/_Cross-cutting/Kutscher_2024_FTSScopingReview.pdf (PubMed Central author manuscript; AM p. = PDF page)

risk_of_bias.note: QUADAS-2 high for both laboratory studies (study cards): Bergh et al.'s readers are not described as blind, its four-level grading was devised after seeing results and its threshold differs from the makers'; Halifax et al. kept only consensus readings and tested lots in separate rounds. Counted once.

inconsistency.note: The two laboratories agree on the pattern (most analogues detected, alfentanil never, carfentanil only at higher concentrations); the review's statement that carfentanil tests negative is second-hand and not counted.

indirectness.note: Pure analogues in laboratory water read by laboratory staff; panels not weighted by what drug markets contain; mixtures untested except one four-analogue mixture on one brand.

imprecision.note: Bergh et al. read one strip per compound and concentration with no replicates, and its table and figure grade the same fentanyl result differently; Halifax et al. used duplicates; Green et al.'s analogue set had four samples.

publication_bias.note: Not assessable from these sources; laboratory evaluations of test strips are not registered.

grade.reasoning: Test-accuracy evidence starts high and is rated down for risk of bias, indirectness and imprecision, so very low. Rated as worded: which analogues these strips reacted to at the concentrations tested, not how often strips would flag analogues in real drug samples. Status replicated: Bergh et al. and Halifax et al. are independent laboratories pointing the same way.
